subject: Vertical migration
topic: The biggest migration on Earth happens every single day, and most people have never heard of it.
script:
The biggest migration on Earth happens every single day, and most people have never heard of it.
Every night, billions and billions of animals swim up from the deep toward the surface.
Small fish, shrimp-like crustaceans and jellies rise up in the dark to feed.
When the sun comes up, they swim back down into the dark, deep waters.
It's called diel vertical migration.
From ships, scientists can even see this crowd of animals on sonar, as a layer in the water.
This journey moves carbon from shallow water down into the deep ocean.
The open water column is the largest habitat on Earth, more than ninety-five percent of our planet's living space.
Did you know this happens every night?
